headline: Bangladesh and China agree to deepen cooperation on Teesta project and river management
summary: The two nations have reached a consensus on enhancing collaboration for the management of the Teesta river and other key water bodies.
details: Bangladesh and China have reached an agreement to strengthen their cooperation regarding the Teesta project and overall river management.
The consensus focuses on leveraging technical expertise and joint efforts to improve the efficiency and sustainability of river systems.
This partnership aims to address critical water management challenges and enhance the environmental health of the Teesta river.
Both countries expressed a commitment to deepening their strategic ties through these infrastructure and environmental initiatives.
caption:
A new strategic push for water security: Bangladesh and China unite for the Teesta project.

Bangladesh and China have reached an agreement to strengthen their cooperation regarding the Teesta project and overall river management.

The consensus focuses on leveraging technical expertise and joint efforts to improve the efficiency and sustainability of river systems.

This partnership aims to address critical water management challenges and enhance the environmental health of the Teesta river.

Both countries expressed a commitment to deepening their strategic ties through these infrastructure and environmental initiatives.

headline: 8.2 million addicts: Govt to arm drug force and set up special courts
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed reveals a massive drug crisis and announces a legislative overhaul to empower narcotics officers and clear legal backlogs.
details: Bangladesh has an estimated 8.2 million drug addicts, driven by the rapid spread of synthetic and semi-synthetic narcotics, according to Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.
The government has approved a Tk 14.13 billion plan to build 200-bed state-of-the-art treatment and rehabilitation hubs across seven divisional cities.
To support private efforts, the ministry is providing Tk 11 million in grants to 73 non-government rehabilitation units.
The Home Minister admitted that Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) officers are currently weaponless, leaving them outmatched by heavily armed drug syndicates.
A new legislative framework is being fast-tracked to parliament this session to allow narcotics officers to be armed and better secure the frontline.
The legal system is severely clogged, with 80,000 narcotics lawsuits pending in Dhaka alone, alongside thousands more in district courts.
To resolve this backlog, the government has proposed the establishment of special tribunals specifically for drug-related offenses.
caption:
8.2 million people in Bangladesh are struggling with drug addiction. Now, the government is planning to arm narcotics officers to fight back.

Bangladesh has an estimated 8.2 million drug addicts, driven by the rapid spread of synthetic and semi-synthetic narcotics, according to Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.

The government has approved a Tk 14.13 billion plan to build 200-bed state-of-the-art treatment and rehabilitation hubs across seven divisional cities.

To support private efforts, the ministry is providing Tk 11 million in grants to 73 non-government rehabilitation units.

The Home Minister admitted that Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) officers are currently weaponless, leaving them outmatched by heavily armed drug syndicates.

A new legislative framework is being fast-tracked to parliament this session to allow narcotics officers to be armed and better secure the frontline.

The legal system is severely clogged, with 80,000 narcotics lawsuits pending in Dhaka alone, alongside thousands more in district courts.

To resolve this backlog, the government has proposed the establishment of special tribunals specifically for drug-related offenses.

Source: bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV, Somoy News
